# Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

User preferences are rapidly evolving and people are increasingly gravitating to generative AI
experiences to help them find information. As we upgrade Search to meet these changing expectations,
this transformation offers new opportunities to reach people who may be more inclined to engage
with your site, spend more time with your content, or even convert by becoming a subscriber or
making a purchase. This guide is for website owners looking for official best practices from Google
Search on how to succeed in generative AI features in Google Search (such as AI Overviews and AI
Mode).

## Is SEO still relevant for generative AI search?

In short, yes! The best practices for SEO continue to be
relevant because our generative AI features on Google Search are rooted in our core Search ranking
and quality systems. These features rely on AI techniques to highlight content from our Search
index, such as:

- Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): A technique (also known as grounding) used to improve the quality, accuracy, and freshness of AI responses by relying on our core Search ranking systems to retrieve relevant, up-to-date web pages from our Search index. Our systems then review the specific information from those retrieved pages to generate a more reliable and helpful response, showing prominent, clickable links to relevant web pages that support the information in the response.
- Query fan-out: A set of concurrent, related queries generated by the model to request more information and fetch additional relevant search results to address the user's query. For example, if the original user's query is "how to fix a lawn that's full of weeds", fanout queries might include "best herbicides for lawns", "remove weeds without chemicals", and "how to prevent weeds in lawn".

> [!IMPORTANT]
> What about "AEO" and "GEO"? "AEO" stands for "answer engine optimization" and "GEO" for "generative engine optimization". These are both terms you may see used to describe work specifically focused on improving visibility in AI search experiences. From Google Search's perspective, optimizing for generative AI search is optimizing for the search experience, and thus still SEO. If you're considering third-party "AEO" or "GEO" advice or services, review our guidance on evaluating third-party SEO advice.

## Apply foundational SEO best practices to generative AI search

This section focuses on reframing SEO best practices to understand what matters most to AI systems
today and how you can implement them in the context of generative AI search, and ultimately with
the goal of improving your website's visibility in both generative AI search experiences and Google
Search overall.

### Create valuable, non-commodity content for your audience

Creating content that people find unique, compelling, and useful will likely influence your
website's presence in generative AI search in the long run more than any of the other suggestions
in this guide. While "unique, valuable, good content" can mean different things to different
people, content like this generally shares some common attributes, such as:

- Providing a unique point of view: Our AI systems take a look at a variety of sources, so it can be helpful to have a unique viewpoint that stands out. For example, a first-hand review provides a unique perspective based on personal experience, whereas a summary of existing content simply restates information already available elsewhere. Create the content yourself based on what you know about the topic, and consider what in-depth experience you can bring to your content. Don't just recycle what others on the internet have already said, or could easily be produced by a generative AI model.
- Creating non-commodity content that's
helpful, reliable, and people-first: Be sure that you're writing non-commodity content that your readers will find helpful and reliable. Commodity content (for example, something like "7 Tips for First-Time Homebuyers") is often based on common knowledge, which could originate from anyone, and typically adds little unique insight for readers. In contrast, non-commodity content (such as "Why We Waived the Inspection & Saved Money: A Look Inside the Sewer Line") provides unique expert or experienced takes that go beyond common knowledge and the ordinary.
- Organizing content in a way that helps your readers: Write content for your human audience and make sure the content is well written and easy to follow. People generally appreciate it when web pages are organized by paragraphs and sections, along with headings that provide a clear structure to navigate content.
- Add high-quality images and video : Many people appreciate finding images and videos as they search for things online. As with Google Search overall, our generative AI search features can bring in relevant images and video, which means more opportunities for your website to appear beyond web page links. When it makes sense, look for ways to support your textual content with high-quality, relevant images and videos on your pages. If you're already following our image SEO best practices and video SEO documentation, you're already optimizing for generative AI search.
- Focus on what your users want, and avoid overdoing it. While it might be tempting to create separate content for every possible variation of how people might search (for example, by focusing on other queries that people have asked, or fan-out queries), doing so primarily to manipulate rankings or generative AI responses in Google Search violates Google's scaled content abuse spam policy. This is also an ineffective long-term strategy, as a high quantity of pages doesn't make a website higher quality or more relevant to users. Google's AI systems have advanced even further and improved upon our ability to understand the relevance of pages, even when there is no exact match between the query and the page's primary content.
- If you're using generative AI tools to assist in content creation , be sure that your work meets the standards of the Search Essentials and our spam policies. For more details on our approach, see our guidance on AI-generated content.

You can simplify your approach by focusing on one core principle: focus on what your visitors
would enjoy, find helpful, and feel satisfied with after visiting your website. If you're ever
unsure about a decision for your site, ask yourself: "Is this content that my visitors would find
satisfying?" If the answer is yes, then you're on the right track, as our systems are designed to
connect people with exactly that kind of useful information. For more, check out our guide to
creating helpful, reliable, people-first content.

### Build and maintain a clear technical structure

The way Google Search finds and processes your pages remains the core of how our AI systems access
your data. Technical clarity ensures your content is ready for discovery and indexing, and all
existing technical SEO best practices
continue to be worthwhile, for example:

- Meet the Search technical requirements: To be eligible to be shown in generative AI features on Google Search, a page must be indexed and eligible to be shown in Google Search with a snippet, fulfilling the Search technical requirements. In addition to the technical requirements for Search, a site must be
included in Search generative AI features in Search Console
to be eligible for display in generative AI features on Google Search. [!NOTE]
Just because a page meets all requirements, best practices, and complies with the policies, doesn't mean that Google will crawl, index, or serve its content. Indexing and serving aren't guaranteed. Learn more about How Search Works.
- Follow crawling best practices . To maximize your site's visibility in generative AI search features, ensure your content is crawlable, as Google Search generative AI models use publicly accessible, crawlable content to learn patterns and provide relevant, grounded responses. For very large and frequently updated sites, review our guide to optimizing your crawl budget.
- When it comes to semantic HTML, focus on human readability and don't worry about
perfect code: While it's not required to have perfectly semantic HTML (the web in general is not valid HTML, and Google can understand it), it's generally a good idea to try to use semantic HTML when possible, as it helps other types of users, such as screen readers, parse and navigate your web page more easily.
- If you're using JavaScript, be sure to follow JavaScript SEO best practices . Google is able to process content within JavaScript as long as it isn't blocked. That said, working on SEO with a website that uses JavaScript frameworks is generally more complex than when working with other kinds of websites. Make sure to follow the usual SEO best practices for JavaScript.
- Provide a good page experience for those who arrive at your site. This includes ensuring your site displays well across all devices, reducing latency, and making it easy for people to distinguish your main content from other elements on the page.
- Reduce duplicate content: Having duplicate content can be a bad user experience and search engines might waste crawling resources on URLs that you don't even care about. If you have time, try to reduce it.

To discover and diagnose potential technical issues quickly, verify your site in Search Console.
For more, check out our technical guide to SEO
and maintaining your website's SEO.

### Optimize your local business and ecommerce details

Where appropriate, generative AI responses can include product listings, product information, and
information about local businesses. Using products like Merchant Center
(such as Merchant Center feeds)
and Google Business Profiles can
help your products and services to be visible in both AI responses and other Google Search
results. Learn more about how to
add and manage your business details on Google Search.

> [!NOTE]
> Depending on your business type and goals, consider other merchant experiences like Business Agent, which is a conversational experience on Google Search that helps customers chat with your brand.

## Mythbusting generative AI search: what you don't need to do

As generative AI search evolves, so have the theories and practices---and sometimes, the
misconceptions---surrounding it. While terms like Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) or
Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) are common online, many suggested "hacks" aren't effective or
supported by how Google Search actually works.

To help you focus on what matters for your website's visibility, we've collected some of the most
prominent topics circulating the internet around generative AI and Google Search. Here are a few
things you can ignore for Google Search:

- LLMS.txt files and other "special" markup : You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, markup, or Markdown to appear in Google Search (including its generative AI capabilities), as Google Search itself doesn't use them. Note that Google may discover, crawl, and index many kinds of files in addition to HTML on a website: this doesn't mean that the file is treated in a special way. [!NOTE]
It's completely fine if you decide to create and maintain LLMS.txt files (or other similar files) for other services or systems that use these files. Doing so will neither harm nor help your site's visibility or rankings in Google Search, as Google Search ignores them.
- "Chunking" content: There's no requirement to break your content into tiny pieces for AI to better understand it. Google systems are able to understand the nuance of multiple topics on a page and show the relevant piece to users. However, sometimes shorter (or longer!) pages can work well depending on your audience and subject matter. There's no ideal page length, and in the end, make pages for your audience, not just for generative AI search.
- Rewriting content just for AI systems: You don't need to write in a specific way just for generative AI search. AI systems can understand synonyms and general meanings of what someone is seeking, in order to connect them with content that might not use the same precise words. This means you don't have to worry that you don't have enough "long-tail" keywords or haven't captured every variation of how someone might seek content like yours.
- Seeking inauthentic "mentions": Just like the rest of Google Search, our generative AI features can show what's being said about products and services across the web, including in blogs, videos, and forum discussions. However, seeking inauthentic "mentions" across the web isn't as helpful as it might seem. Our core ranking systems focus on high-quality content while other systems block spam; our generative AI features depend on both.
- Overfocusing on structured data: Structured data isn't required for generative AI search, and there's no special schema.org markup you need to add. However, it's a good idea to continue using it as part of your overall SEO strategy, as it helps with being eligible for rich results on Google Search.

## Measure visibility in generative AI features with Search Console

To measure how your content is performing in generative AI features on Google Search and
Discover, use the Generative AI performance report
in Search Console. This can help you get an idea of how people are discovering your content through
generative AI features on Google Search.

> [!CAUTION]
> Be wary of third-party tools that promise ranking success or claim to use "internal" Google metrics. No third-party tool has access to our internal ranking or AI systems. Use these tools if they help your workflow, but be sure to evaluate their advice against our official guidance.

## Explore agentic experiences

AI agents are autonomous systems that can perform tasks on behalf of people, such as booking a
reservation or comparing product specifications. These agents can take many forms; for example,
browser agents may access your website to gather the data they need to complete these tasks, such
as analyzing visual renderings (like screenshots), inspecting the DOM structure, and interpreting
the accessibility tree.

If this is something that's relevant to your business and you have extra time, check out the
available agentic experiences and review the guide to
agent-friendly website best practices,
which gives some insights into how a website can generally prepare for current browser agents.
Protocols like Universal Commerce Protocol
(UCP) are emerging that will allow Search agents to do more.

## Next steps: what to focus on

As you continue working on your website, remember that plenty of content thrives in Google Search
(including generative AI experiences) without any overt SEO at all, and you don't need to
accomplish everything in this guide in order to succeed on Google Search. To recap, here are the
key takeaways from this guide:

- Apply SEO best practices to generative AI search: Continue prioritizing foundational SEO best practices, such as building a clear technical structure and creating unique, valuable content; these are the foundation for visibility in generative AI search experiences (and Google Search overall).
- Create non-commodity content that's helpful, reliable, and people-first: Focus on developing unique, expert-led content that provides value beyond common knowledge.
- Prioritize effective SEO strategies over "AEO/GEO hacks": For Google Search, you can ignore tactics like "chunking" content, creating unnecessary AI text files (like llms.txt), or pursuing inauthentic mentions.
- Monitor visibility in Search Console: Use the Generative AI performance report to see how your content is performing in generative AI features on Google Search.
- Explore agentic experiences: Stay informed about emerging technologies that allow AI agents to interact with your site, such as browser agents and new protocols.

## Stay informed and ask questions

If you want to learn more about SEO, here are some resources that can help you stay on top of
changes and new resources we publish:

|---|---|---|
| | - Google Search Central blog: Get the latest information from our Google Search Central blog. You can find information about generative AI in Search, new Search Console features, and much more. - Google Search Central on LinkedIn and X (Twitter): Follow us for updates on Google Search and resources to help you make a great site. | - Google Search Central Help Forum: Post questions about your site's SEO issues and find tips to create high quality sites from the product forum for website owners. There are many experienced contributors in the forum, including Product Experts and occasionally Googlers. - Google Search Central YouTube Channel: Watch hundreds of helpful videos created for website owners. |

# Google AI Mode & AI Overviews: What They Mean for Your SEO in 2026

In 2026, zero-click searches have risen to 68%. Part of this is because of the evolving user behavior. But primarily, it can be attributed to the new AI search features.

People are still getting answers, but not via the traditional blue links anymore. AI mode and AI overviews have entered the equation, and they are here to change not just search but SEO as well. The search visibility doesn’t primarily lie in rankings now; it also centers on optimizing for AI search features as well.

We created this guide to help you stay visible in AI search. It covers:

Google AI mode SEO & retrieval methods.

The changes Google AI features are likely to bring to the search.

How to optimize for better visibility in AI mode?

## What is Google AI Mode?

AI mode is an AI-led search feature offering an end-to-end search experience. It works similarly to ChatGPT in practice. You search for something, and AI directly answers the query without you having to navigate through ten different URLs. Of course, the answer integrates inline links and citations for source references.

Recently, with the introduction of Gemini 3.5, the search box went through major changes. It was the first upgrade in 25 years and was led by the AI search features, including AI Mode. The most notable changes are:

The search box now expands to allow longer queries.

You can also follow up on an AI Overview answer right from the SERPs.

The search page transitions seamlessly into AI Mode with a follow-up post.

### Why was AI Mode introduced?

AI Mode started showing up in people’s search experiences in early 2025, the year Sundar Pichai encouraged his team to focus “on unlocking the benefits of this technology and solve real user problems.”

It was part of a plan to reclaim their position after LLMs like ChatGPT and Perplexity started claiming a big chunk of their traffic. Naturally, Google wanted to align its search experience with the evolving user behavior. And hence, they introduced AI Overviews and, shortly after, AI Mode.

AI Mode vs AI Overviews: What’s the Difference?

AI Mode is actually an extension of AI Overviews. When you search on Google, AI Overviews appear at the top of the results page, whereas AI Mode takes you to a different search window where you can continue a conversation via AIOs.

Here’s how it works in practice.

To put this difference into perspective, AI Mode reshapes the search session into a conversation, while AI Overviews replaces blue links with a synthesized answer above them. How Does AI Mode Generate Answers? Google’s AI features use two retrieval methods: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) RAG technique is used to ensure answers are accurate and up-to-date. While Google’s AI Mode primarily relies on Gemini’s training data, it also integrates RAG technology to extract relevant pages from the search index in real time and use them as grounding material to generate responses. This is why your pages should be indexed and crawlable to earn citations.

Query fan-out

When a user submits a query, Google’s AI doesn’t just search for that exact phrase. It retrieves from a set of concurrent, related queries to answer from a broader context window.

From Google’s own example: ‘..if the original user’s query is “how to fix a lawn that’s full of weeds”, fanout queries might include ‘”best herbicides for lawns”, “remove weeds without chemicals”, and “how to prevent weeds in lawn”.’

Simply put, it collects information from a number of related queries to synthesize an answer that serves the intent in a broader context.

### How AI Search Retrieval Differs From Organic Search

Specific sections from content can be retrieved to answer a sub-question, independent of how the full page ranks.

A single query fans out into numerous related searches behind the scenes before a response is generated.

Content is pulled from multiple sources and synthesized into a single response.

Individual search history and behavioral signals influence how the same query gets answered for two different users, while traditional results will almost always show the same listings.

Being cited matters as much as being clicked. Content can influence a response without generating a measurable visit to the source page.

Multi-modal system where queries can trigger text, images, videos, and audio in the same tab.

## How is Google AI Mode Impacting SEO?

With Google’s AI Mode getting a huge chunk of space in the SERPs, it’s safe to say organic search has been altered irrevocably. For brands to retain visibility in the new search era, it’s important to understand how Google’s AI features affect organic traffic so they can align their SEO decisions based on evolving search behaviors.

For reference, position one CTR has dropped by 34.5% for queries resulting in an AI Overview. Users are much less likely (8%) to click on a blue link for queries with an AI summary.

But all that is just scratching the surface. It’s also important to understand that Google’s AI features behave differently from traditional search ranking systems. While the core retrieval principles might be the same, SEO in the AI era has certainly evolved.

Industry-Wise Impact

Here are some common stats to highlight the highest and lowest impact of Google AI Mode and AIOs on specific industries.

AI Overviews show up for 82% of B2B tech queries.

Healthcare queries get an 88% share of AI summaries.

Education queries trigger AI features for 83% of the time

AI Overviews trigger far less frequently for local searches and navigational queries

## How To Appear In AI Mode & AI Overviews

Getting down to the important question, which SEO strategies should we adopt to get cited in Google AI Mode and AI Overviews? While the standard rules of quality content and brand authority apply here, some adaptations have to be made to conform to the new search landscape.

Some ranking factors in 2026 impact Google AI mode visibility more than others. Let’s review what they are.

### The content side of things—what works and what doesn’t

AI Mode rewards the same thing as traditional SERPs: good writing and helpful content that matches user intent. Here is a list of key practices when optimizing content for visibility in the AI search feature:

Share real experience, genuine expertise, or a perspective that goes beyond the obvious. An expert’s review on a niche topic, an original research study, or a blog that doesn’t just provide information but integrates an element of personalization is a great way to get your content noticed.

Structure it so that it’s easier for a human to read. Clear headings, logical flow, and well-written paragraphs combined with other content formats (images, videos, etc.) when they are helpful.

Don’t try to cover every search variation. Writing a separate page for every way someone might phrase a query is against Google’s spam policies, and it doesn’t work. A single, yet thoroughly written page on a topic will outperform a dozen thin ones any day.

Don’t misuse AI tools to mass-produce low-quality pages that offer no real value to users. Any content produced using AI should conform to Google’s standards for helpful, reliable, and people-first content.

Remove any duplication across the site to make sure similar pages do not dilute page authority or waste crawl budget.

#### What doesn’t work

Two things that don’t work according to Google’s official guidelines on AI optimization:

Content Chunking – Breaking content into shorter paragraphs or sentences. Google doesn’t need bite-sized pieces to understand your page. The content length should reflect your topic and your audience’s capability to comprehend it.

Rewriting content for AI – Changing tone, structure, or topics solely to help AI understand it is not a smart strategic move. Google explicitly mentions, “You don’t need to write in a specific way just for generative AI search.”

### The importance of E-E-A-T and original research

Google’s AI prefers quality content, and its algorithm system assesses quality based on EEAT. Ahrefs confirms this with the statement:

“EEAT is an acronym of a framework Google uses to evaluate content quality.”

Any content demonstrating Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness automatically has a higher likelihood of getting featured in the SERPs. And that includes AI features as well. It can pick up on signals that a human wrote something from lived experience, not just from research.

Here are some tactics that increase citation likelihood:

Named authors with verified credentials.

Original data and proprietary research.

Specific, verifiable claims.

Community and platform authority.

What significance do communities carry in this regard? Reddit holds 21% of AIO citations. AI overviews and AI mode also frequently cite LinkedIn and other communities, making this strategy critical when optimizing for AI mode.

### Leverage Images & Videos

Google’s generative AI search features actively pull in relevant images and videos alongside web page links, which means your visuals now have their own shot at surfacing in search results. Google also pointed this out in its AI optimization guide.

“…our generative AI search features can bring in relevant images and video, which means more opportunities for your website to appear beyond web page links.”

And if you’re already following Google’s image SEO best practices and video SEO guidelines, you might just be optimizing for generative AI search as well. So supporting written content with strong visuals isn’t extra work; it’s more content for AI to cite.

### Redirect Focus to Brand Mentions

Mentions from authentic sources are critical and help amplify a brand’s voice across various search surfaces, including AI-generated responses. A study by AirOps highlights that 85% of AI mentions come from external domains, while only 13.2% of mentions come directly from the brand’s domain. The study offers a clear correlation between AI search visibility and brand mentions.

There’s one condition, though. The mentions should come from authentic sites that wish to link to you because of the quality of your content. Inauthentic mentions have no value for AI search visibility. Google addresses this in the following words:

“...seeking inauthentic “mentions” across the web isn’t as helpful as it might seem.”

Note that earning brand mentions differs from traditional PR or link building, as it involves naturally earning recognition across the web without a direct link placement.

### Technical SEO: a good hack for AI SEO

When most people think about optimizing for Google’s AI features, they jump straight to content. However, no amount of great writing will help if Google can’t find, crawl, and index your pages in the first place.

Technical SEO determines whether your content is even eligible for AI citations.

And here’s how you can optimize for it.

Start with indexability. A page must be crawlable and indexable, the two basic eligibility criteria to appear in Google Search, before it can even be considered for generative AI features. Also, make sure your pages aren’t blocked by robots.txt.

Apply proper semantic HTML as it helps screen readers and other tools navigate your pages. It’s a good practice, but there’s no need to overdo it because Google crawlers can also read invalid HTML.

If your site relies on JavaScript frameworks, follow established JavaScript SEO best practices. Google can process JavaScript content as long as it isn’t blocked, but JS-heavy sites do add a layer of technical complexity worth addressing. Ensure critical content is pre-rendered or server-side rendered. Client-side rendering adds delays to indexing.

Page experience remains relevant. Factors such as fast speed, mobile-friendly design, and a clean layout where users can easily identify your main content all contribute to how Google evaluates your pages.

#### Bonus Point

Schema markup helps in specific cases (reviews, FAQs, how-tos), but it’s not required for AI citation. Focus on foundational SEO first: crawlability, indexability, and quality content. If you have resources remaining, implement schema for rich results.

## How to Measure AI Data on GSC

Google confirmed in a June 2026 report that you can now view search data for AI Overviews and AI Mode via Google Search Console. This gives you direct visibility into how often your content is being cited and how many impressions it’s earning through these AI-powered features.

To isolate AI search data, follow these steps:

Open the Performance report in GSC.

Under Search Results, find Generative AI. This will isolate data for AI Overviews and AI Mode only.

At the moment, you can only view impressions. Clicks, ranks, and CTR are not part of this report.

You can narrow down your search by pages, devices, countries, and dates.

Note that this feature is only in the testing phase and may take some time to be widely available. However, if it pans out, the data is quite promising and will provide a whole new analytics stream for AI mode and AI overviews.

It will provide critical visibility into AI citation performance: a measurement gap that currently exists.

And that’s all there is to know about Google AI mode and AI overview optimization at the moment. The foundation stays the same: quality content, technical excellence, and authentic authority. Focus there first, then adapt as Google’s AI features change.

As the strategies evolve, make sure you’re staying updated and following through for best results.

## What Is Generative AI SEO?

Generative AI SEO is the practice of making your content readable, trustworthy, and citable by AI systems that synthesize answers rather than return ranked lists. The shift from ranking in a list to becoming the answer is not a small adjustment - it changes what good content looks like at a fundamental level.

Here's what's happening under the hood: traditional search engines match keywords to pages and return links. Generative AI systems work completely differently. They tokenize your HTML, move content into vector space, find semantically relevant passages across multiple sources, and then synthesize a coherent answer. Your page might be cited without the user ever clicking through to it.

What this means for brands is direct: if your content isn't structured to be cited, you're invisible to an estimated 40% of online information-seeking sessions (early 2026 estimate). That's not a traffic dip - that's a structural gap in your discovery funnel.

## Generative AI SEO vs Traditional SEO: What's Different in 2026

The differences aren't subtle. Here's a clear comparison across the factors that matter most:

| Factor | Traditional SEO | Generative AI SEO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goal | Rank on a search results page | Be cited in an AI-generated answer |
| Primary Platform | Google, Bing | ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Mode |
| Success Metric | Rankings, organic traffic | AI Citation Frequency, AI Share of Voice |
| Key Ranking Factor | Backlinks, keyword optimization | Structured content, E-E-A-T, entity signals |
| Content Format | Keyword-rich, long-form pages | Answer-first, extractable, schema-marked |
| Link Signals | High weight - backlinks drive authority | Moderate - brand mentions and citations matter more |
| Freshness Weight | Medium | High - stale content loses citations quickly |
| Measurement Tool | Google Search Console, Ahrefs | OptimizeGEO, GA4 AI referral tracking |

One important nuance: Google AI Overviews have the strongest correlation with traditional SEO - 76.1% of URLs cited in AI Overviews rank in the top 10 organic results. So if you rank well, you're likely to be cited there. ChatGPT operates differently, drawing from a much wider source pool. For the full breakdown, see GEO & SEO Best Practices 2026.

## Why Generative AI SEO Is Non-Negotiable in 2026

The scale of AI search adoption makes this impossible to deprioritize:

- ChatGPT has 800M+ weekly active users - and a significant portion use it for product research, comparisons, and recommendations
- Google AI Overviews now appear in 55% of all Google searches - meaning more than half of all Google queries are now partially answered by AI before a user sees a single organic link
- AI-referred traffic from ChatGPT grew 206% in 2025 (Search Engine Land)
- AI-referred visitors browse 12% more pages and have a 23% lower bounce rate than non-AI referrals (Adobe) - they're high-intent buyers who already had their question partially answered by AI

That last point is the one that changes the ROI conversation. Traffic that arrives via AI citation is pre-qualified in a way that most other channels aren't. See how this plays out in practice in the Global Beauty Brand AI Visibility Case Study.

## 7 Core Generative AI SEO Best Practices

### 1. Answer-First Structure with a Quick Answer Box

Lead every page with the direct answer in the first 2-3 sentences. AI systems pull from the top of a page first - if the answer isn't immediately visible, your content gets skipped for something cleaner. Adding a formatted Quick Answer or TL;DR box at the top of key pages is a simple, high-impact structural change that significantly improves citation eligibility.

### 2. Triple Schema Markup - FAQPage + Article + HowTo

Stacking schema types on a single page is legitimate and recommended. FAQPage schema makes your Q&A sections directly eligible for AI-generated FAQ responses. Article schema signals publication context, authorship, and freshness. HowTo schema works for process-based content. Use JSON-LD`@graph` format to stack these cleanly without conflicts.

### 3. E-E-A-T Signals - Author Credentials, Original Data, Expert Quotes

Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness aren't just Google's guidelines - they're signals that most AI citation systems use to evaluate whether a source is worth quoting. In practice, this means: named authors with verifiable credentials on every piece of content, original research or proprietary data where possible, and quotes from recognizable experts or institutions. Content without clear authorship is treated as less citable across most LLMs.

### 4. Topical Authority - Cover Every Sub-Question on Your Topic

AI systems don't just retrieve pages - they break complex questions into sub-queries and pull from the best available source for each part. If your site covers the main topic but leaves sub-questions unanswered, a competitor fills those gaps and gets cited instead. Build out complete topic clusters that address every natural question a user might ask within your category. Intent-Based Modeling is a useful framework for mapping this out.

### 5. Content Freshness - Quarterly Updates with Visible Timestamps

Stale content loses citations. AI platforms - Perplexity in particular - actively weight recency in their source selection. A quarterly review cadence for core pages is the minimum: update statistics, refresh examples, re-publish with a visible new date. For the full cadence model, see the GEO Success Glidepath (90-Day Roadmap).

### 6. Entity Building - Consistent Brand Mentions Across Reddit, LinkedIn, Wikipedia

AI systems develop citation confidence about brands that appear consistently across multiple credible, independent sources. A brand mentioned only on its own website is less citable than one mentioned across Reddit discussions, LinkedIn posts, Wikipedia, Crunchbase, and industry publications. Entity building means actively managing where and how your brand is described across the web.

### 7. Technical AI Accessibility - llms.txt, Unblocked AI Crawlers, Fast Core Web Vitals

If AI crawlers can't access your content, none of the above matters. Check three things: (1) your`robots.txt` is not blocking`GPTBot`,`ClaudeBot`, or`PerplexityBot`; (2) you have an`llms.txt` file at your root domain guiding AI crawlers to your priority pages; (3) your Core Web Vitals scores are strong. The Prepare Website for LLM Searchability guide covers all three in detail.

## How to Optimize for Google AI Mode (2026)

Google AI Mode launched in May 2025 for all US users and is powered by Gemini 2.5. Understanding how it differs from AI Overviews matters because the two features behave differently and need to be optimized for independently.

Key differences:

- AI Mode handles more complex, multi-part queries than AI Overviews - it's built for research-style questions
- AI Mode returns an average of 12.6 links per answer vs 13.3 for AI Overviews
- Only 13.7% of citations overlap between AI Mode and AI Overviews - meaning content cited in one is frequently not cited in the other

Practical optimization for Google AI Mode:

- Ensure full mobile optimization - AI Mode surfaces heavily on mobile search
- Implement`BreadcrumbList` schema to help Gemini understand your site hierarchy
- Cover topic breadth - AI Mode pulls from multiple sources to answer multi-part questions
- Maintain strong organic rankings as a baseline

Voice search accounts for 30% of all AI answer engine interactions - and it's powered by the same sources as text-based AI search. Siri, Google Assistant, and Alexa pull from AI-generated answer layers that use the same citation logic as their text counterparts.

Voice-specific optimization factors:

- Conversational heading structure - headings should read like natural spoken questions, not keyword strings
- Q&A format throughout - structure content as questions followed by direct answers
- Short sentence length for extracted answers - aim for under 20 words per sentence in sections most likely to be pulled as a voice response
- Speakable schema markup - the`SpeakableSpecification` schema tells AI assistants which sections are formatted for voice delivery

The practical overlap between voice and AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) is almost complete - if your content is structured to be cited in a text AI answer, it's almost certainly structured for voice delivery too.

## FAQs

### What is Generative AI SEO?

Generative AI SEO is the practice of optimizing content and brand presence so that AI-powered search systems - ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Perplexity, Gemini - cite, recommend, and synthesize your content in their answers. It differs from traditional SEO in that the goal is to become part of an AI-generated answer, not just to rank on a results page. It requires structured content, E-E-A-T signals, schema markup, and entity authority.

### Is traditional SEO still relevant in the age of generative AI?

Yes - it's still the foundation. Most AI platforms pull from search indexes, so pages that aren't indexed can't be cited. Google AI Overviews cite top-10 organic results 76.1% of the time, so strong rankings remain a prerequisite for that surface. The shift is that rankings alone are no longer sufficient. Generative AI SEO layers content structure, schema, and authority signals on top of the traditional SEO base - it doesn't replace it.

### What are AI SEO best practices for 2026?

The core AI SEO best practices are: answer-first content structure with Quick Answer boxes, stacked schema markup (FAQPage + Article + HowTo), strong E-E-A-T signals through author credentials and original data, topical authority across complete content clusters, quarterly content freshness updates, entity building across Reddit and LinkedIn and Wikipedia, and technical AI accessibility via llms.txt and unblocked crawlers. Applied together, these consistently improve AI citation rates.

### How do I optimize for Google AI Mode?

Google AI Mode uses Gemini 2.5 and handles more complex multi-part queries than AI Overviews. To optimize: ensure full mobile optimization, implement BreadcrumbList schema, build broad topic clusters rather than single-page depth, and maintain strong organic rankings as a baseline. Importantly, only 13.7% of citations overlap between AI Mode and AI Overviews - so the two need to be treated and measured as separate optimization targets.

### What is the difference between Generative AI SEO and GEO?

They describe the same discipline from slightly different angles. GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) is the broader category term - coined by Princeton researchers in a 2024 paper. Generative AI SEO is used more often by practitioners with an SEO background who are extending into AI search. In practice, the strategies, tactics, and metrics are identical. Both focus on getting your brand cited in AI-generated answers rather than ranked on traditional results pages.

### How much does Generative AI SEO affect organic traffic?

The effect is significant and growing. With 69% of searches now zero-click and Google AI Overviews appearing in 55% of all searches, traditional organic click-through rates have declined materially - position 1 sees a 58% CTR reduction when an AI Overview is present. However, AI-referred traffic, while lower in volume, converts substantially better - Adobe data shows 12% more pages browsed and 23% lower bounce rate.

### How does E-E-A-T apply to Generative AI SEO?

E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) matters more in generative AI SEO than in traditional SEO because AI systems are actively evaluating source credibility before deciding whether to cite. In practice: every piece of content needs a named, credentialed author; original data and research signals genuine expertise; quotes from recognized experts or institutions add authority; and consistent brand mentions across credible third-party sources build trustworthiness.

# Optimizing Content for Google AI Overviews (2026): A Practical Guide for Content Creators

By Deidre Donnelly

•

This year, many digital marketers and content creators are still grappling with how to adapt to AI Overviews (AIO), the biggest shift in Google search since the original PageRank algorithm. With searchers skipping traditional SERPs in favour of AI’s fast results requiring fewer clicks — and recent research by BrightEdge showing that the presence of AI Overviews grew to nearly half ( of the queries they tracked over a year — it’s clear that content strategies must go beyond SEO, and include visibility tactics such as GEO and AEO.

If you’re a content creator, learning how to appear in AIO should be a key goal for 2026. To help you ensure your brand stays relevant in this game-changing AI search landscape here we provide 10 top techniques to increase your chances of getting cited within AI Overviews, boosting your brand’s AIO “share of voice”.

As we outlined in a previous blog, Google’s AI Overviews (powered by Gemini) deliver summarised answers drawn from several sources at or near the top of search results, reducing the need to click through to individual pages. This has naturally hit organic traffic hard, with recent research by Ahrefs showing that the presence of an AI Overview correlates with a 58% lower average click-through rates (CTR) for the top-ranking page (though this varies according to query type and vertical). With the race to get recognised on Google now intensified, here are 10 ways to align your content to AI crawler preferences

In another blog, we explained why (E-E-A-T) is the most important framework for helping get your brand’s content picked up by AI crawlers. As AI agents assess whether you have the relevant experience and inside information on your topic, you need to prove your authority. The best way to illustrate the potential effectiveness of amplifying your E-E-A-T efforts is through the below instructive case study:

After Google’s March 2024 algorithm update, HubSpot experienced an alarming 70–80% decline in organic traffic (2024 — 2025). Their content was devalued by not aligning closely enough with their core offerings. Their top-of-funnel topics had strayed from their main CRM platform service.

So they focused on optimizing for inclusion in AI citations. Some of the strategies they used tie into E-E-A-T:

They developed content written by practitioners with actual experience and informed perspectives.

: They pruned irrelevant content and aligned topics with their main services. They also used “” sentence structures to write standalone statements that AI crawlers could easily read.

: Schema markup was used to identify the professional contributors and their organisation. In addition, HubSpot boosted their community and third-party presence (using PR, Wikipedia updates, Reddit threads, etc.).

HubSpot writers spent more time refreshing old content than generating new posts, while keeping canonical URLs. This helped the LLMs register their site as credible enough to cite.

A remarkable turnaround that included a , and fourth place on Semrush’s AI Visibility Index(for the business and professional services vertical).

Google’s AI responses tend to fall into four main categories:

1. Discovering new subject matter
2. Instructions, How Tos and troubleshooting tips
3. Gathering opinions for informed decision-making
4. Product comparisons

Consider the main questions your potential customers would ask within each category. Then create content that answers their queries as clearly as possible.

Content should also be written conversationally. With more users searching using natural language and AI picking up on this in its responses, you should . Address questions in natural-sounding language that cuts to the chase.

- Give succinct answers that directly respond to queries.
- Provide 40- to 60-word ‘ answer capsule’ summaries at the top of article sections, so that AI can draw from them.
- Include FAQ and clearly mark them as such using FAQ schema.
- Use question-based subheadings.
- Consider other questions that may pop up under “” — the most common SERP feature, according to Search Engine Journal’s STAT whitepaper on SERPS (April 2026) — and answer them in your content. Thanks to the “query fan-out” technique AI systems use, this broadens the range of queries you could be cited for.

Structured data helps AI systems parse, index and understand your content contextually. Schema markup feeds Google’s Knowledge Graph, improving your chances of appearing in AI-generated summaries. Use annotations wisely, and be sure to for the content to improve your chances of getting noticed. Nested schema structures are also a smart move, as these create entity relationships that AI detects when searching for authoritative results.

- FAQPage and HowTo
- Article or BlogPosting
- Organisation and Person (for E-E-A-T signals)
- Product (especially for e-commerce pages)

- Label important details like author, topic and publishing date clearly
- Implement Article schema, How To schema, etc.
- Use Google Search Console (GSC) Structured Data Reports to check your schema coverage

Another way to earn a spot in an AI-featured snippet is to pay attention to how your content is structured.

Use a clear heading structure that flows logically. Be sure to incorporate question-based long-tail keywords into subheadings. Each sub-section should contribute to the overall article, but also be capable of standing alone.

Don’t bury the answer in a long blog with an overly long introduction. Lead with the answer in an easy-to-parse format (e.g. short-form answer, list, definition, how-to). Thereafter, place all the important information at the beginning of each content section. Flesh the explanation out after. This not only saves the hurried user from unnecessary scrolling, it makes it more likely that AI will scan your content.

Think including a table of contents, bullet points, numbered lists, H2 and H3 headings, and FAQ at the end.

AI models are multi-modal. Since AI pulls from more than just text, it’s best to add multimedia assets to your content. Ideas include:

- Adding more images with relevant descriptive alt text and captions
- Summarising information in infographics, short videos, charts and diagrams
- Including interactive elements like calculators, carousels and quizzes
- Adding video sitemaps to help the search engine index your video content

Google’s Core Web Vitals provide the baseline for checking your page quality. Slow-loading pages are less likely to be trusted by AI crawlers, so optimize all images with descriptive alt text, compress files for fast loading and ensure your content renders correctly across all screen sizes.

In one example from Search Engine Land, a large enterprise cloud platform faced a projected 79-85% drop in organic traffic due to AIO changes.

By optimising 11 pages with multimedia-rich content and AI-focused design, eight of those pages entered the AI Overview panel, reversing the expected traffic loss and saving 17 strategic keywords from losing visibility.

Building topical authority is one of the most reliable ways to earn AI citations A topic cluster strategy built around pillar pages and supporting content.

Create a pillar page around a topic that’s core to your brand. Then create multiple content pages that support the cornerstone content through internal linking. These cluster pages can explore the topic from multiple angles. This also reinforces your entity relationships (associations between your brand, experts and content topics), as the more you’re linked with relevant topic clusters, the more authoritative you appear. Note that the pillar page should link to the supporting content pages; the cluster pages should link back to the cornerstone page.

You create a pillar page about “Personal Finance” for your finance brand, with links to cluster such as:

- How to create a monthly budget
- Tips for building an emergency fund
- Understanding credit scores and how to improve them

SEO tactics still matter. So keep your technical SEO on point to make it easy for AI systems to crawl, index and understand your content.

- Eliminate performance issues that slow down your site’s page load speed.
- Fix crawl errors and broken links to ensure AI systems and users don’t encounter dead ends.
- Ensure your website structure is clean with clear hierarchies for greater AI crawlability.
- Implement HTTPS and secure your site to build trust and meet Google’s security preferences.
- Leverage XML sitemaps and robots.txt to guide AI crawlers efficiently through your site.
- Include conversion rate optimization (CRO) in your SEO strategy. This is because, as the 2024 Google API leak showed, Google’s internal Navboost feature tracks and uses clicks as a ranking signal that search engines use to assess pages for ranking.
- Audit your robots.txt for AI crawler directives. Blocking crawlers protects your content from AI training, but it may cost you citation visibility. Content and developer teams should weigh up this trade-off.

AI systems like comprehensive content that’s current. They assess things like byline dates, URL dates and timestamps showing when the page was last updated. Regularly refreshing existing posts is often more effective than publishing new ones.

- Refresh old posts with updated links, statistics, case studies or insights.
- Add the date of publication and/or update.

Do regular performance testing of your AIO optimization efforts:

- Do a manual SERP analysis to check when your content appears in Google’s AI Overviews or AI Mode, not just traditional organic rankings.
- Track your AIO “share of voice” with tools like Semrush’s AI Toolkit or Ahrefs’ AI Visibility feature to monitor branded and unbranded AI Overview appearances against competitors.
- Monitor user engagement signals (such as time on page, scroll depth), as these may inform how AI systems assess content quality and relevance.
- Track changes in click-through rates (CTR): Since AIO can reduce traditional organic clicks, track CTR shifts carefully to adjust your content and calls-to-action accordingly.
- Use data from Google Search Console’s performance reports combined with third-party tools to correlate AIO visibility with traffic and rankings.

Stay updated on Google’s AIO and AI Mode feature rollouts and algorithm updates. With Google describing AI Mode as the future of search, it’s one to watch. The fully conversational interface breaks queries into sub-questions, synthesising answers from across sources, which is sure to raise the bar in terms of becoming a citable authority.

By now it’s clear that in the age of AI search, content creators and strategists should be http://admin.digivate.com/blog/seo/sxo-vs-seo-why-search-experience-optimisation-is-the-future/. Content optimization must go beyond just Google’s AI search and keep all AI platforms in mind, including Perplexity, Microsoft CoPilot and ChatGPT.

While Google’s AIO creates new challenges for driving organic traffic, it also opens opportunities for content creators and brands willing to adapt their strategies. Success in the AI-first search depends on offering helpful content, leveraging structured data and building genuine authority. So start implementing these Google AIO SEO best practices today to be ahead of the competition tomorrow.

Browse through our others, including “ How to Rank in Google AI Overviews in 2026: What Gemini Really Looks For.”

Google uses AI to provide comprehensive answers from multiple sources at the top of search results, reducing the need for users to click through to individual websites.

Focus on creating well-structured, authoritative content that follows E-E-A-T principles, uses schema markup, answers questions clearly and includes multimedia elements with proper alt text.

How-to guides, FAQ content, comparison articles, and well-structured informational content with clear headings and concise answers tend to perform well.

Use tools like Semrush and Google Search Console to track when your content appears in AI overviews, monitor changes in CTR and analyse user engagement metrics.

# How to Optimize Your Content for Google AI Overviews

- Contact

Search has changed in a big way. For those who have been practicing SEO for a while now, it is a fact that ranking on page one was your end goal. But in 2026, your end goal has changed. Now, you will find out that something is placed just above these ten blue links. It is called Google AI Overviews, and if your content is not showing up there, a large chunk of your audience may never even scroll down to see your website.

This guide provides you with a precise definition of Google AI Overviews optimization, its significance for your business, and the exact steps you should take to get your website into such summaries generated by AI technology. Whether you operate a small business, manage the digital presence of a brand, or are preparing for a career in digital marketing, this is what SEO looks like in 2026.

### What Are Google AI Overviews and How Do They Work?

### What Are AI Overviews?

Google AI Overviews are AI-generated answer boxes that appear at the very top of Google search results. They were previously called the Search Generative Experience (SGE) before Google rolled them out widely. With the development of AI technologies, when a user enters a query in Google, he/she can find not just a set of links to pages containing the answer to his/her question; Google offers a pre-written answer based on artificial intelligence. Under this answer, there are links to pages that served as sources of information for Google’s algorithms.

Such answers are designed to reduce the search time of a user. Google uses several websites to gather the information and then compiles it into one easy-to-understand answer. For users, this is beneficial, but for businesses, this process requires additional efforts.

### How AI Overviews Work: Understanding RAG and Query Fan-Out

AI Overviews’ technology is referred to as RAG; Retrieval-Augmented Generation. What this means is that Google’s AI does not fabricate the answer; rather, it first searches for information in its live index and identifies the most reliable websites before generating the response. The sources are shown as clickable link cards, which is how websites still get traffic from these summaries.

There is another concept worth knowing here: query fan-out. As for queries regarding complicated topics such as “how to fix a lawn with weed problem,” instead of simply trying to find information on the specific question, Google’s AI algorithm takes the query apart into several other sub-queries that might include “best weed killers for the lawn,” “weed removal without chemicals,” and “how to avoid weeds.” Understanding this helps you write content that covers a topic deeply rather than just answering one narrow question.

### When and Where Do AI Overviews Appear?

Not every search shows an AI overview. As of 2026, they are visible for around 5% to 15% of all searches. They tend to be shown more frequently for informational or research purposes, as well as for health and technological issues. For example, when people are asking “how to begin a digital marketing career” or “which CRM is better for freelancers,” then chances are that an AI overview will show up. However, for shopping and brand searches, they do not appear too frequently because they are ad-driven and navigational-oriented.

### The Impact of AI Overviews on Google Search and SEO

#### Why AI Overviews Matter So Much

The biggest issue with AI overviews is real estate. They sit at the very top of the page, above all organic results. If an AI Overview is present and your site is not cited in it, users have to scroll past the entire AI block before they even see your link. On mobile, this means most users may never reach you at all.

The advantage of featuring in the AI Overview section is that even before someone decides to make any clicks, your brand becomes visible. This makes you the spokesperson in the commercial rather than the small print at the end.

### Will Organic Traffic Go Down Because of AI Overviews?

Honestly, yes, for top-of-funnel informational queries. Research tracking AI Overviews’ prevalence shows organic click-through rates dropping significantly on queries where an AI summary appears. Some studies have reported drops of around 30% to 60% in CTR for affected queries.

However, there is hope. The traffic that actually comes through is of far greater value. Someone who goes through an AI summary, finds the citation and ends up on your page really needs your product or service. It is no longer someone casually surfing online, he/she is looking for something to consume. He/She is ready to read, purchase, subscribe, contact, or register.

### Is SEO Still Relevant for Generative AI Search?

Absolutely. According to Google’s own documentation, generative AI search features are built directly on top of their core search ranking systems. The AI does not find sources from some separate pool. It pulls from the same search index that standard SEO has always targeted. Studies show that nearly all of the pages cited in AI Overviews come from the top organic results. You must rank organically first to have any chance of being cited in the AI summary. So SEO is still relevant, more than ever, in fact.

### How to Optimize for AI Overviews: A 6-Step Strategy

## Summary
In 2026, Google’s generative AI experiences in Search—AI Overviews and AI Mode—are reshaping visibility, with official guidance emphasizing helpful, people-first content and clear structure over any “AIO hacks” [1][7]. Third‑party playbooks converge on building topical depth, structuring content for extraction, and monitoring performance via the AI Mode appearance in Search Console to stay part of AI-generated answers amid rising zero‑click behavior [2][3][4][5][6][8].

## Key Findings
1) Google has issued official guidance for optimizing content for generative AI features in Search, including AI Overviews and AI Mode, centering on helpful, reliable, people‑first content rather than tricks targeted solely at AIO [1][7].

2) Zero‑click behavior has increased sharply in 2026, reinforcing the need to be included in AI-generated answers: estimates cite ~68% zero‑click searches [2] and 69% with rapid growth in AI‑assisted queries [3].

3) Content most likely to be surfaced/cited in AI Overviews is clear, concise, and structured for extraction, while demonstrating E‑E‑A‑T (experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trust): answer‑first sections, scannable formatting, practical steps, and first‑hand insights are repeatedly stressed [1][3][4][5][6].

4) Covering query “fan‑out” via topical clusters—mapping related intents, follow‑ups, and entities—and interlinking them is recommended to increase your brand’s chance of selection across AI Overviews and AI Mode conversations [3][4][5][6].

5) Semantic HTML and structured formatting (descriptive headings, lists, tables) are advised to help Google’s AI features parse, summarize, and cite the right segments of your pages [1][4][5][6].

6) Tracking: Google Search Console exposes an “AI Mode” option in the Search Appearance filter so you can monitor impressions and clicks attributable to AI experiences [8].

7) There is no separate “AIO ranking system” you can directly game; aligning with Google’s quality guidance remains the recommended path to visibility in AI Overviews and AI Mode [1][7].

## Detail
Official stance and implications
- Google’s developer guidance explicitly addresses optimization for generative AI features in Search (which includes AI Overviews and AI Mode), positioning it as an evolution of Search that rewards helpful, people‑first content. The focus is on meeting user needs comprehensively and reliably, not chasing AI‑specific loopholes [1]. Industry leaders also flagged this as Google’s official guidance for AIO/AI Mode optimization [7].
- Practically, this means reinforcing E‑E‑A‑T, giving users clear and direct answers, and structuring information so Google can understand and reuse it in generative summaries [1].

The changed traffic model in 2026
- Multiple analyses note the rise of zero‑click searches tied to AI experiences and shifting user behavior. Reported 2026 levels vary—68% [2] and 69% [3]—but both underscore the same strategic point: if your brand isn’t part of the AI‑generated answer, you lose exposure even if you “rank” traditionally [2][3].
- Guides frame generative AI search as moving from “ranking in a list” to “being the answer,” requiring content that’s readily extractable and authoritative [3][4][5][6].

How to appear and get cited in AI Overviews
- Emphasize answer‑first writing and scannable formats: concise summaries high on the page, step‑by‑step instructions, FAQs that anticipate related user intents, and clearly segmented sections help AI Overviews pick precise snippets to cite [4][5][6]. 
- Demonstrate E‑E‑A‑T and helpfulness throughout: practical, first‑hand experience; clear guidance; and content that addresses user goals comprehensively are repeatedly highlighted as elements AIO tends to reward [1][3][4][5][6].
- Use semantic HTML and structured formatting: descriptive H2/H3 headings, lists, and tables make content easier for AI systems to parse and summarize, improving inclusion odds [1][4][5][6].
- Build topical authority with clusters: cover the core topic plus the query’s likely “fan‑out” (related intents, follow‑ups, and adjacent entities), and interlink across the cluster. This positions your site to be cited not only for the initial query but also subsequent AI‑driven conversational steps [3][4][5][6].
- Align content to user tasks and formats AI Overviews often present: practical guides, comparisons, pros/cons, and step‑by‑step walkthroughs show up across recommendations as formats that perform well in generative summaries [3][4][5][6].

Query fan‑out and topical clusters
- Generative AI experiences expand and refine queries conversationally. Guides recommend anticipating this “fan‑out” by planning clusters that address the main question plus related subtopics, alternative methods, troubleshooting, and decision criteria. This increases the likelihood of your domain being referenced across a chain of AI‑assisted interactions [3][4][5][6].
- Internal linking and consistent on‑page structure across the cluster help AI systems connect your related resources and select the strongest page for a given facet or follow‑up [3][4][5][6].

E‑E‑A‑T and helpful, people‑first content
- Google’s guidance emphasizes helpfulness and reliability; E‑E‑T principles matter for generative AI just as for traditional search [1]. 
- Third‑party frameworks suggest highlighting first‑hand experience, practical evidence, and clear authoritativeness to increase the chances of being used as a cited source in AI Overviews [3][4][5][6].

Semantic HTML and structural signals
- Multiple sources encourage semantic structure: clear headings mapping to specific sub‑questions, bulleted/numbered lists, and tables for comparisons or steps. These patterns help AI extract ready‑to‑quote segments and align with Google’s general guidance on making content understandable to Search features [1][4][5][6].

Measurement and monitoring
- In Google Search Console, you can filter Performance → Search Results by Search Appearance and select “AI Mode” to analyze impressions and clicks from AI experiences. This provides a way to monitor AI‑related visibility alongside traditional metrics [8].

What content is winning in 2026’s AI experiences
- Practical, task‑oriented content that is concise, structured, and demonstrates experience is emphasized across guides as more likely to be surfaced in AI Overviews: clear “what/why/how,” comparisons, step‑by‑steps, FAQs, and content that anticipates follow‑ups [3][4][5][6].
- Given Google’s stance, this aligns with producing helpful, reliable, people‑first content rather than optimizing solely for a snippet [1][7].

A pragmatic workflow (synthesized from the sources)
- Qualify intents that trigger AIO/AI Mode for your topics; note the formats AI highlights (definitions, steps, comparisons) [3][4][5][6].
- Build topical clusters that cover fan‑out (FAQs, alternatives, troubleshooting), interlink pages, and keep answer‑first sections prominent [3][4][5][6].
- Reinforce E‑E‑A‑T and present information with semantic HTML (headings, lists, tables) to maximize extractability [1][4][5][6].
- Track AI Mode in Search Console and iterate on pages that earn impressions but few clicks, refining summaries and task‑completion support [8][3][4][5][6].

## Gaps / Caveats
- Metrics vary: zero‑click share differs across sources (68% vs 69%), and growth figures for AI‑assisted queries are not independently corroborated here; treat them as directional, not definitive [2][3].
- Opaque selection: Google’s official page doesn’t disclose the specific mechanisms used to select/cite sources in AI Overviews; most tactical guidance is inference‑based from practitioners and tools, not a formal specification [1][2][3][4][5][6].
- Guarantees: None of the sources provide guaranteed inclusion criteria for AIO; recommendations focus on aligning with quality and structure best practices rather than deterministic controls [1][4][5][6].
- Tracking scope: The Search Console “AI Mode” filter enables monitoring AI experiences broadly, but the sources do not detail granular differentiation among specific AI surfaces (for example, isolating only AI Overviews) [8].
